assertions.head_surface: Documents containing maintenance requirements for systems, equipment items or components
assertions.applicability: marine machinery reliability and maintenance surveys
assertions.evidence_text: Documents containing maintenance requirements for systems, equipment items or components are to be reviewed at least annually to identify outdated maintenance processes, techniques or technologies, or to bring attention to obsolete tools and outdated spare parts.

assertions.applicability: marine machinery reliability and maintenance surveys
assertions.evidence_text: Task packaging reviews should be conducted periodically to evaluate the packaged maintenance intervals to verify that as maintenance tasks are added, deleted or modified, optimum packaged intervals are maintained.

assertions.tail_surface: insufficient age-to-failure data are available or assumed data are used during the initial reliability based analysis
conditions: When insufficient age-to-failure data are available or assumed data are used during the initial reliability based analysis
assertions.applicability: marine machinery reliability and maintenance surveys
assertions.evidence_text: When insufficient age-to-failure data are available or assumed data are used during the initial reliability based analysis, age exploration tasks are to be designed and implemented.

auxiliary.statement: Task packaging is the process of bundling a number of derived maintenance tasks into optimum uniform intervals such as maintenance performed during a vessel’s scheduled dry-docking.
auxiliary.reason: Definition of a maintenance planning concept; not directly representable as a relation between defined node types without inventing nodes.
auxiliary.evidence_text: Task packaging is the process of bundling a number of derived maintenance tasks into optimum uniform intervals such as maintenance performed during a vessel’s scheduled dry-docking.

auxiliary.statement: An effective reliability based program will necessarily impose frequent changes to an age exploration program, such as adding new equipment, deleting completed or unproductive tasks, or adjusting task intervals.
auxiliary.reason: Program management guidance; no specific pump component or fault target on this page to form a concrete assertion edge.

auxiliary.statement: The result of the age-exploration tasks is a better understanding of the system or equipment’s wear-out region of the failure characteristics curve, which can be fed back for use in updating the analysis.
